I tested forty IT stocks. Only seven passed. The rules: profit up twenty percent a year, and almost zero debt.
Coforge and RateGain grew fast, but borrowed big. MapmyIndia's profit barely moved. So who made it?
NPST runs UPI software for banks. Profit up eighty four percent a year. Zensar serves banks in the US, Europe and Africa, up thirty four.
Aurionpro runs metro ticketing and banking software, up thirty. Persistent builds AI software, up twenty eight.
Affle sells mobile ads, up twenty three. Newgen sells software to banks, up twenty two. eMudhra makes digital signatures, near twenty two.
Three almost passed. Netweb builds AI servers, up sixty four percent, but carries some debt. Zaggle and Unicommerce have only two years of history.
Now the catch. Passing is not a buy signal. Persistent's profit fell twenty five percent last quarter, after an acquisition. NPST trades at seventy nine times profit.
And look where the money comes from. eMudhra earns sixty six percent abroad. From the US to Kenya to Kazakhstan.
